bluf: Mod Op is an independent US connected creative agency with 450+ specialists and ten offices, selling brand, content, PR, data, CRM and digital experience work to enterprise brands on top of ORION, its AI platform. It is moving fast: ORION unveiled in 2026-07, a free AI search visibility audit and the GEO 50 benchmark in 2026-08, and No. 16 on ADWEEK's 2026 Fastest Growing Agencies list in 2026-09 on 189% revenue growth. The record points it at AI transformation sold as creative. A rival should know it sells AI visibility with no llms.txt, runs no ads of its own in either library, and 10 of 14 clients are names only.
doing:
The positioning line, a connected creative agency powered by its Orion AI platform blending creative talent and intelligent technology, decodes as a creative group that has rebuilt its pitch around a proprietary AI layer. The headline claim is growth: No. 16 on ADWEEK's 2026 Fastest Growing Agencies list after 189% revenue growth, plus No. 1781 on the 2026 Inc. 5000 (202% three year growth); CEO Eric J. Bertrand sits on the 2026 ADWEEK 50.

The sold mix leads with AI Automation / Agents, score 3: the Orion powered homepage, an AI Solutions line, and the Mod Agent and AI Risk Intelligence launches. Five core lines score 2. AI Search / GEO: the free audit, the GEO 50 benchmark, the GEO Periodic Table framework and 18 AI search URLs. Content & Digital PR: Strategic Communications and Content pages, plus the Copyleaks earned coverage case. Data & Measurement: Data + Martech Enablement and Market Intelligence with 30+ researchers. Email & CRM: the Nokia global marketing automation case and the Ascend Marketing acquisition. Web & Product: a Digital Experience page covering UX, web development and QA, plus site builds. Paid search, paid social, local and retail media score 0, although Media Management is a listed service.

AI posture: everything runs on ORION and AI is sold as products, roadmaps, brand aware agents, risk auditing and the free GEO audit at geo.modop.ai.

Moves in date order: 2024-12 acquired Image Media for live events; 2025-06 a $5M AI investment; 2025-08 joined the Shopify Partner Program, its one partner; 2025-10 acquired Ascend Marketing; 2026-03 launched AI Risk Intelligence; 2026-07 unveiled ORION and hired David Doyle; 2026-08 the free audit, the GEO 50 and the Inc. 5000 place; 2026-09 the ADWEEK ranking.

The record lists no pricing model. Conspicuously absent for a 450+ person agency with a Media Management line: any ad of its own in either library, any paid media score, and an llms.txt.
clients:
The ICP is enterprise and nine verticals are listed, CPG & food, Beverages & spirits, Entertainment & gaming, Travel & hospitality, Technology & telecom, B2B information services, Energy & utilities, Agriculture and Ecommerce; the home market is the US with offices in Miami, New York City, Los Angeles, Dallas, Kansas City, Philadelphia and Cleveland, plus Toronto, Calgary and Panama City.

The needs read holds 14 clients, 11 from case studies and 3 from slugs, with 4 observed and 10 names only. Brand and creative leads the mix at 0.432: Duracell came for a brand activation and John Deere for an autonomous tractor launch, both from slugs, and Copyleaks for positioning as a leader in AI image detection (brand with AI). AI and automation sits at 0.341 and CRM and owned audiences at 0.227, both carried by Nokia, whose case describes marketing automation at global scale. The names only: Sparkling Ice, Enbridge Gas, Verizon (a public sector impact slug), American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE), Warner Bros. Interactive (a lego star wars slug), Dietz & Watson (a site build per the Web & Product note), Baha Mar, Travel Alberta, Reyka Vodka and Panera Bread; need inferred from what the agency leads with, AI solutions and brand.

Three clients are shared: Verizon with publicis-sapient and ayima, Duracell with vaynermedia and John Deere with the-goat-agency.

What the base needs next: the read places Mod Op best for KJ4, the platforms are absorbing the execution layer, and KJ1, the click is being replaced by the citation, with no headwind listed. It is likely, moderate confidence, that these enterprises next buy AI visibility audits and automation on top of brand work, the direction of its 2026 launches, and roughly an even chance they ask it to run paid media it does not score on.

openings:
Lead with the llms.txt contradiction: Mod Op sells AI visibility, publishes a GEO 50 benchmark and a free audit, and its own site has no llms.txt. A rival that publishes one and shows its own citation share very likely, moderate confidence, wins the credibility test with a buyer who runs the free audit on both sites. Falsifier: an llms.txt appearing on modop.com.

The paid gap is the second opening: Media Management is a listed service while paid search and paid social score 0 and no ad of its own appears in either library, so a rival with a visible performance program likely takes the media budget of its brand clients, low confidence on how much it holds today. No feed, schema or entity work appears on its search or web lines (P2 absent): the machine readable layer beneath its GEO framework is unclaimed.

Contestable clients: the 10 names only and the three that shop, Verizon (publicis-sapient, ayima), Duracell (vaynermedia) and John Deere (the-goat-agency). With no public pricing model (P5 unknown), a transparent outcome priced offer is a conversation it cannot have in public.
